title: Conflicts of interest and the quality of recommendations in clinical guidelines
authors: Cosgrove L, Bursztajn HJ, Erlich DR, Wheeler EE, Shaughnessy AF
journal: Journal of Evaluation in Clinical Practice
population: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients with Major Depressive Disorder (2010), its development group, independent review panel and cited references
funder: not read: the publisher full text is behind a paywall, no archived copy was found, and Crossref metadata list no funder.
result: All members of the guideline development committee disclosed financial ties to industry, a mean of 20.5 relationships (range 9 to 33), most on speakers' bureaus; members of the independent review panel had undeclared financial relationships. 44.4% of studies supporting recommendations met criteria for high quality, 34.2% of cited research did not study outpatients with major depressive disorder, 17.2% did not measure clinically relevant results and 19.7% of references were not congruent with the recommendations; 13% of references supporting recommendations were co-authored by the six developers. Results read from the abstract.
